decisions.mark: names MBEDTLS_THREADING_C and MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD as the gating macros
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "`MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is commented out at `include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h:3787` (`//#define MBEDTLS_THREADING_C`). `MBEDTLS_THREADING_ALT` and `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` are also commented out" and "With `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` + `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD`" | WHY: The answer names both macros as the ones controlling whether mutexes/locking are compiled in (the section header and the "Mutexes exist only when `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is enabled" statement), which covers the gating-macros item.

decisions.mark: states that the shipped mbedtls_config.h leaves BOTH threading macros undefined, so a default build defines neither
decisions.detail: QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is commented out at `include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h:3787` (`//#define MBEDTLS_THREADING_C`). `MBEDTLS_THREADING_ALT` and `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` are also commented out (lines 2185, 2196). | WHY: The answer states the shipped header leaves the threading macros (THREADING_C, ALT, and PTHREAD) commented out, so a default build defines none of them.

decisions.mark: concludes that a default build of mbedtls creates no threads at all, and that the pthread example compiles to a stub main under that condition
decisions.detail: QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer says the library spawns no threads and lists `ssl_pthread_server.c:277` as a spawn site. It never says the pthread example compiles to a stub main in a default build.

decisions.mark: states BOTH halves of the contrast: that nothing in library/ creates a thread, AND that library/ nonetheless supplies the mutex abstraction used by threaded callers
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The four thread-spawn sites the index finds are all in `programs/` (`ssl_pthread_server.c:277`, `benchmark.c:430/444`, `ssl_server2.c:1699`). The library spawns nothing. | WHY: The answer says the library spawns no threads, but it describes the mutex abstraction as conditional on `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C`. It never says that library/ supplies the mutex abstraction (threading.h/threading.c) for threaded callers to use, so the second half of the contrast is missing.
